title: Can a Person Be Arrested Without a Court Warrant in Ethiopia?
description: I want to understand the rules in Ethiopia regarding arrest without a court warrant. In what situations can the police arrest a person without first getting a warrant from a judge? What rights does the arrested person have after being taken into custody? How quickly must the person be brought before a court, and what happens if the police keep the person longer than the law allows? Also, can evidence collected after an unlawful arrest be used in court?

answers.content: Under Article 49 and 51 of the Ethiopian Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), arrest without warrant is an exception permitted only for flagrant offenses (እጅ ከፍንጅ) or where the suspect is reasonably suspected of a grave offense punishable by rigorous imprisonment exceeding 3 years and is likely to abscond. Under FDRE Constitution Article 19, the suspect must be informed immediately in a language they understand of the reasons for arrest and must be brought before a court within 48 hours. Evidence obtained as direct fruit of unlawful arbitrary arrest can be challenged and suppressed under constitutional due process standards.

If police hold an individual past the 48-hour constitutional deadline without securing a formal remand order (የጊዜ ቀጠሮ) from a bench judge, the family or legal counsel should immediately petition the Federal High Court for a writ of Habeas Corpus to compel the station commander to produce the detained person and show lawful cause.

title: Commercial Lease Lockout by Landlord Without Court Order in Addis Ababa
description: My landlord in Bole, Addis Ababa locked the business premises without prior court notice following a 2-week rent dispute.

answers.content: Under Article 2945 and 2946 of the Ethiopian Civil Code and Commercial Code principles, landlords cannot exercise extrajudicial self-help evictions or padlock doors without a valid, enforceable court execution decree. You are entitled to petition the Federal First Instance Court for an emergency possessory restoration order (የይዞታ መመለሻ አቤቱታ) and claim consequential damages for business interruption.

title: Can police hold a suspect in detention for more than 48 hours without a court remand?
description: My cousin was detained by local police on Friday afternoon on suspicion of property damage. They told the family he cannot see a judge until Tuesday because of the weekend. Is this legal under Ethiopian law?

answers.content: Under Article 19(3) FDRE Constitution, court appearance within 48 hours is mandatory.

No, this is a clear violation of constitutional rights. Under Article 19(3) of the FDRE Constitution, every arrested person MUST be brought before a court of law within 48 hours of arrest. Duty judges operate over the weekend for remand hearings. You should immediately retain an advocate to demand immediate appearance or release.

title: What happens to common property in divorce if the house was built on leased land?
description: My husband and I are separating after 8 years of marriage. We built a G+1 house during our marriage on an urban lease plot that was registered in his name only. Am I entitled to half the house value?

answers.content: Yes, absolutely. Under Article 62 and 63 of the Revised Family Code (Proclamation No. 213/2000), any building or immovable improvement constructed during the subsistence of marriage is legally presumed to be common marital property (የጋራ ንብረት), regardless of whose name appears on the lease certificate. The court will order an independent certified engineering valuation for equal equity division.

Make sure you immediately file for an injunction order (የእግድ ትእዛዝ) at the Federal First Instance or High Court to prevent any unauthorized sale, transfer, or bank mortgage on the property while the divorce is pending.

title: Can a One-Person Company (OPC) have foreign investment under the 2021 Commercial Code?
description: I am a foreign investor exploring opening a tech consultancy in Addis Ababa. Can I register a One-Person Company (OPC) without local Ethiopian nominee partners?

answers.content: Yes, under the revised Commercial Code of Ethiopia (Proclamation No. 1243/2021, Article 534), a single shareholder can form an OPC with limited liability. However, as a foreign national, your entity must also comply with the Investment Proclamation No. 1180/2020 minimum capital requirements (typically $200,000 USD for 100% foreign ownership, or $150,000 USD if in joint venture with a domestic investor).

In addition, if your technology consultancy qualifies under the Ethiopian Investment Commission (EIC) special tech incentive schedule, you can register through the EIC one-stop service portal with streamlined foreign currency repatriation rights.

title: My employer terminated my contract after 70 days without written notice. What can I claim?
description: I was hired as a senior accountant on probation. After 70 calendar days, the manager verbally told me not to come back on Monday. They refuse to pay my final month salary.

answers.content: Under Article 11 of Labour Proclamation No. 1156/2019, the maximum probation period in Ethiopia is strictly 60 working days. Because you worked past 60 days without written termination, you automatically attained permanent employee status. A verbal dismissal without written notice and lawful grounds is an unlawful termination (ያለአግባብ ስንብት). You are legally entitled to: 1) Full unpaid wages; 2) Severance pay; 3) Compensation for unlawful dismissal equal to up to 3 months' salary.

title: How is municipal expropriation compensation calculated for private residential property?
description: The City Administration has notified our neighborhood of urban redevelopment expropriation for a road corridor. How is replacement cost and displacement compensation determined under current proclamations?

answers.content: Under Expropriation of Landholdings for Public Purpose Proclamation No. 1161/2019, compensation comprises three separate statutory components: 1) Full replacement cost of all buildings, structures, and trees at prevailing market material/labor rates without depreciation deduction; 2) Displacement assistance equal to 1 year of equivalent rent; 3) Provision of a substitute residential land plot or condominium housing allocation.

title: What is the legal foreclosure procedure for mortgaged collateral by private commercial banks?
description: Our trading enterprise obtained a business loan secured by warehouse property. We experienced an export delay of 45 days. Can the lending bank auction the property immediately without going to court?

answers.content: Under Property Mortgaged or Pledged with Banks Proclamation No. 97/1998 (as amended), commercial banks in Ethiopia possess statutory extrajudicial foreclosure powers (የባንክ ቀጥተኛ የሀራጅ መብት). However, the bank must strictly serve a written default warning notice giving at least 30 consecutive days to settle arrears, followed by certified public newspaper auction notices. If the bank fails to adhere to statutory appraisal and notice periods, you can seek injunctive relief from the Federal High Court.
